recipes.name: Steak Soup
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds lean boneless beef round steak, cut into cubes
1 (15.25 ounce) can whole kernel corn, drained
1.5 cups peeled, diced Yukon Gold potatoes

steps.text: Melt butter and oil in a large skillet over medium heat until the foam disappears from butter. Cook and stir beef and onion in butter-oil mixture until browned, about 10 minutes.
While beef is cooking, mix together flour, paprika, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. Sprinkle flour mixture over browned beef; stir to coat and set aside.

Pour beef broth and water into a large soup pot. Stir in parsley, celery leaves, bay leaf, and marjoram. Stir in beef mixture; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover the pot, and simmer, stirring occasionally, until meat is tender, about 45 minutes.

Mix in corn, potatoes, carrots, celery, and tomato paste. Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender and soup is thick, 15 to 20 minutes. Remove bay leaf and serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Steak Soup
raw_recipe.description: This steak soup is rich and hearty with chunks of tender round steak, potatoes, carrots, celery, and corn simmered in a flavorful tomato-beef broth.

review.reviewBody: I am thrilled to be the first review. This soup was EXCELLENT! I love soup but have always struggled with veggie/tomato/beef based ones. They just never turn out like I remember mom making. Not until this one that is. I made exactly as written and was very pleased. This would be good with some green beans or peas for added nutrition and color too. Very good full bodied flavor and this will be my go to veggie soup. Thank you so much for sharing!

I should have more carefully read the reviews for this before making it. I would have either cut WAY down on the tomato paste, or completely omitted it. I was really excited about this soup as I was making it and then when I added the tomato paste, it turned the nice beef broth into a very strong tomato broth. If you love a strong tomato flavor to your steak soup, then this is a great recipe for you. If i make this again, I will definitely omit the paste. Otherwise, this would be a wonderful recipe.

Very tasty and easy soup to prepare. As with many other reviews I cut back on the amount of the tomato paste and I myself left out the potato and am not a fan of marjoram. Rather than using 2 different pots for cooking, I browned the steak first, then sauteed the rest of the veggies in the pot. I added the tomato paste, broth and a bit of salt and pepper to the mix. Let the flavors meld and served the soup with grilled cheese sandwiches.

My 1 pot variation with what i had on hand was fantastic on a cold wet day! I used leftover smoked ribeye steak from last night, so i skipped 2nd pan. I added 1 large onion (sliced halves) and mushrooms to carrots, celery, in large dutch oven with oil/butter. Saute about 10 min. Med-Hi heat. Added 3 TBSP minced garlic and tomatopaste. Stir. 2 min. Add spices and flour Stir. 2 more min. Pour in LOW SODIUM beef broth and water. Bring to a boil. Add potatoes, corn, bay leaves. Simmer low for 15 mins. Add chopped leftover steak (cooked last night). Turn off heat and let the meat warm a few mins while you get bowls and spoons out. Enjoy! I substituted oregano for marjoram (had none). I also added 1 tsp red pepper flakes.

I love this recipe! I had expensive steak left over. I don’t like left over steak cooked or warmed but this was the exception. I did make some minor adjustments to the recipe after reading the reviews. I browned the onions as directed for 10 minutes but only braised the left over steak for a minute or 2. Also, because the meat was cooked, I brought it to a boil and added the veggies. I only cooked veggies and meat for 20 minutes. Also did not use flour and no water - just beef stock. I did a little paste but not 6 ounces. hubby who is a little fussy liked it too

I thought this was very good, but I did make a couple of changes (yeah, I hate it when posters do that too). I'm staying with my daughter at the moment, she didn't have marjoram or parsley, so I subbed oregano. I added 1 tsp. of garlic powder (I add garlic to just about everything), only used 2T of the tomato paste. It never thickened up, but I did throw everything in the crockpot, instead of cooking on the stove top. Next time, I'll use a bit more beef and potatoes. Still, worth the time and effort.

Great! I used the same recipe, few things I changed was I added the veggies (diced two tomatoes and didn’t have corn) and cooked them a bit with the tomato paste , then added potatoes and broth and meat mixture. My tomato paste was more on the side of a sauce so it worked out better, for those that have an actual paste you will read other comments saying how it ruined it. Make sure to trust your instincts! Loved this soup and it was a great way to use up the veggies in my fridge.

I loved this soup. It is packed with veggies and has a great flavor. Based on other reviews, I seasoned the meat with salt & pepper before cooking, I replaced the tomato paste with a rich pinot noir, and I added 2 portabello mushrooms. Next time I'll add more mushrooms because they are perfect in this soup, and I will chop the veggies and beef a bit smaller. Great recipe!

I loved this, I had some leftover london broil so it came together really quickly. I followed another reviewers suggestion and used 3 tblsp of spaghetti sauce and added some zucchini, yellow sqash, mushrooms and carrots that I had on hand and everyone loved it
Was a delicious base - coated the steak in the flour and shook it up before browning it, I added in some red wine for deglazing and some extra potatoes. Tastes even better the next day!

This was very tasty...although after reading reviews, I did make these changes: eliminated the tomato paste and substituted a 15 oz. can of diced tomatoes. Also added 2 additional cups of beef broth and a tablespoon of Worcestershire Sauce...(that really kicked it up a notch!) I like a thick soup except for beef vegetable soups...much prefer a brothy soup.
Great recipe sound like a keeper
Was rather bland.
My husband loves this soup. The only addition is Worcester sauce, about one tablespoon. Cheers!
Yum!
Great fall weather soup!
This recipe was on the money. We all were happy to eat This well prepared soup .
As many others suggested, I limited the tomato paste to 2 tablespoons. I also added some mushrooms. A tasty stew-like soup. Enough to share with my neighbor!

Like others, I made this with left over steak. I start by using the oil and butter and sautéing onion and garlic, add in the flour and spices to make a roux, then add the broth water and veggies and any additional seasonings to cook the veggies. When veggies are tender, I throw in the corn and the meat and heat it all up again. A wonderful soup to "open" the fall soup season.

This soup is a fan favorite for the over 80 year old crowd. I add mushrooms, peas, green beans and some red wine. It freezes well and is a great meal to give to people who are sick, old or just had a Baby. Just add cookies and a loaf of good bread and it’s a winner!
